co_other_mothers.blurb: Other Mothers is a wall on the left side of the big Mother's Buttress cliff in Unaweep Canyon, in the Grand Junction area of western Colorado. The cliff rises to roughly 450 feet at its tallest, so a few lines go multi-pitch, but most are a single rope length. Of the 17 climbs here, about twelve need a rack and five are bolted. Grades start around 5.5 and climb to 5.11, with a good chunk of 5.8 to 5.11 in the middle, so it suits solid intermediates as well as people just stepping up. Expect cacti near the base and some loose rock, so helmets are wise.

co_lower_security_risk.blurb: Lower Security Risk is a crag in Boulder Canyon above Boulder, Colorado, at around 7,400 feet and one of three buttresses that make up the Security Risk Massif. It sits above Happy Hour Crag and mixes steep crack lines with a handful of bolted routes; roughly twelve of its 17 climbs are trad and five are sport. Most pitches run 50 to 100 feet, with one two-pitch line. Grades mostly fall from 5.10 to 5.13, with a few easier at 5.8 and 5.9 and one harder outlier, so this is a better fit for experienced climbers. The massif faces south and is known as a winter destination.
